text: 🇲🇽🎨 17,878 pieces of looted heritage, brought home. Since the Fourth Transformation began, Mexico has recovered 17,878 archaeological and historical artifacts from abroad — 3,700 of them under President Sheinbaum alone, in one year and nine months. For scale: that is more than ten times what was repatriated under Peña Nieto, and already 68% of everything Calderón recovered in six full years. No purchases. No ransoms. A patient diplomatic campaign built on one principle: looted heritage belongs to the people it was taken from — not to auction houses.

🇲🇽🌎 Washington declined to renew the USMCA. Mexico isn't panicking. July 1 was the deadline for the three partners to extend the trade pact to 2042. The United States chose not to renew it in its current form — which triggers annual reviews rather than termination. The treaty stays in force for another decade. Trump's stated grievance is the U.S. trade deficit; his instrument has been tariffs on steel, aluminum, and autos. Mexico's answer has been to keep negotiating — on its own terms, without confrontation. Through every tariff threat, Sheinbaum has repeated the same line: “siempre defenderemos la soberanía e independencia de México” — “we will always defend the sovereignty and independence of Mexico.” Mexico is now the United States' top trading partner. The dependence runs both ways.

🇲🇽🇻🇪 Mexico sent 264 soldiers to earthquake-hit Venezuela. They came home with Venezuela's highest honor. After the June 24 earthquakes, Mexico's “Yumare” military group — 264 personnel and 18 canine teams — deployed to Venezuela. They rescued 2 people, recovered 92 bodies, and provided 2,059 medical consultations. “Ustedes mostraron el verdadero rostro de México: un México solidario, fraterno y profundamente humanista.” “You showed the true face of Mexico: a Mexico of solidarity, fraternity, and deep humanism.” “Ninguna vida es ajena… esa es la esencia del pueblo de México: no dejar a nadie atrás.” “No life is foreign to us… that is the essence of the Mexican people: to leave no one behind.” — President Claudia Sheinbaum, receiving the Yumare group, July 10, 2026 Venezuela awarded Sheinbaum its highest distinction, “Hero of Venezuela, First Class.” The brigade returned home with Laika, a six-month-old Belgian shepherd gifted to the Mexican Army.

🇲🇽🌎 THE PLAYBOOK: US NARCO-ACCUSATIONS AS A LEVER TO WEAKEN LATIN AMERICAN GOVERNMENTS

From Noriega onward, Washington has wielded drug-trafficking accusations to destabilize governments it dislikes across Latin America. Mexico reads the script: Sheinbaum frames the current "narco" pressure as injerencia meant to weaken sovereign states — the same logic that once drove Iran-Contra. Her line holds: cooperation on information, never subordination.

🔥🇲🇽 SHEINBAUM ON CALDERÓN'S US-BLESSED DRUG WAR: "IT WAS A STATE OF EXCEPTION"

Sheinbaum drew the contrast in numbers: daily homicides climbed from 28.6 in 2006 to 70.9 by the end of Calderón's term — a "war on drugs" she called "un régimen de excepción." That era's Operation Fast and Furious walked more than 2,000 high-caliber US weapons straight into cartel hands. Her government now reports over 50,000 arrests and a sharp fall in daily homicides.

🚨🇲🇽 "OPERATIONS IN MEXICO CAN ONLY BE CARRIED OUT BY MEXICAN INSTITUTIONS": SHEINBAUM

On Washington's push to put its own agents on Mexican soil, Sheinbaum was flat: "Las operaciones que se realizan en nuestro país solamente las pueden hacer las instituciones mexicanas." Collaboration means shared intelligence — not foreign operatives running raids. "Si colaboramos y ustedes nos dan información, nosotros operamos." Cooperation without subordination.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 "NO TO MILITARY AGGRESSION AGAINST CUBA" — 8,840 SIGNATURES, 58 COUNTRIES

Months after President Sheinbaum floated a hemispheric declaration against military intervention in Cuba, the international manifesto against a US attack on the island has gathered 8,840 signatures across 58 countries — Elena Poniatowska, Silvio Rodríguez, Daniel Jiménez Cacho and Laura Esquivel among them. It names the danger plainly: the warmongering escalation of Trump and Marco Rubio.

July 8, 2026 | 🟢

The Peterson Institute does the math on killing USMCA: a ~92% tariff pass-through to shoppers and a 2.7% jump in US auto prices. "Punishing" Mexico is really a tax on American wallets.

95.7% of US transport-vehicle imports come from Mexico and Canada — there is no version of this where US consumers don't foot the bill.
